rationale: The data to answer the question already exist in the call logs, the outcome is defined by time stamps, and the decision needs a description of where delays occur and which factors go with them. A retrospective review of two years of logs, with the interval fixed from verification to documented read-back (c2), benchmarked against published call-log analyses (c1), and with night staffing (c4) and call attempts as named factors, answers it without new data collection. Reporting follows STROBE with the RECORD extension.
alternatives: Prospective observation of notification for three months (refused: slower, smaller and changes behaviour while observed)
Trial of an escalation route (deferred: the review first shows whether delays are concentrated where an escalation route would act)
whyNotMoreComplex: Existing time-stamped logs answer a descriptive question directly; a prospective or experimental design would add cost and delay without improving the answer the director needs.

decision.statement: Conduct the retrospective review of the 2024 and 2025 call logs, measuring notification from verification to documented read-back against the 30-minute standard and reporting delays by location, time of day, analyte, night staffing and call attempts.
decision.question: Should the laboratory measure critical value notification from its call logs before deciding on an after-hours escalation route?

criteria.text: Call-log analyses can measure notification reliably from verification to read-back.
Delays are plausibly concentrated in outpatient, community and night results where an escalation route or staffing change would act.
The extract lacks location or read-back fields for a large share of calls.

gates.requirement: Research ethics board approval with waiver of consent
gates.evidence: REB file 26-311 approved 2026-08-27, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Agreement to provide a de-identified call-log extract
gates.evidence: Data request LIS-DR-2026-19 agreed 2026-09-02, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Introduce an escalation route without measurement
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1, c2 and c4 from retrieved records; both gates are met on investigator-supplied records.

summary: Retrospective review of call logs recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and both gates are met.
